headline: MV June Aster Death Toll Rises to 76 as 13 Remain Missing
seoTitle: MV June Aster Ferry Fire Death Toll Rises to 76 | FMB News
seoDescription: The confirmed death toll in the MV June Aster ferry fire off Coron has risen to 76, with 13 people still missing as identification and investigation continue.
deck: Authorities recovered more remains from the burned MV June Aster, raising the confirmed death toll to 76 while 13 people remain missing and investigators work to establish the cause of the fire.
author: FMB News Desk

continuesFrom.headline: Ferry Fire Off Coron Leaves at Least 5 Dead as Search Continues
continuesFrom.whatChanged: Since FMB News first reported at least five deaths, rescuers have gained access to the burned ferry and recovered dozens of additional remains. The confirmed death toll has now risen to 76, with 13 people still missing.

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The confirmed death toll from the MV June Aster ferry fire off Coron, Palawan has risen to 76 after rescuers recovered more remains from the burned vessel on Saturday, September 12.
Reuters reported 76 confirmed deaths, 43 survivors and 13 people still missing. Associated Press independently reported the same death toll and missing-person figure.
The passenger ferry caught fire on September 9 while nearing Coron after sailing from Manila. Authorities are continuing victim identification and the investigation into how the fire started.

sections.heading: What changed since FMB's first report
paragraphs: FMB News first reported the disaster on September 10 when authorities had confirmed at least five deaths and rescue teams were still unable to fully search the vessel because of heat and smoke.

A September 11 continuation documented the recovery of 30 additional bodies and a death toll of 35. The latest recovery raises that toll to 76, making this a separate material continuation rather than a silent update to the earlier reports. Both earlier articles remain intact.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The ferry's original manifest listed 117 passengers and 17 crew members. Authorities later determined that two people on the manifest had not actually boarded, bringing the reconciled number aboard to 132.
The latest accounting reported by Reuters and AP is 76 dead, 43 survivors and 13 still missing, which totals 132 people.

Survivors have described hearing explosions before the fire spread, but no final official finding has established the cause or point of origin. FMB News is not treating those accounts as a determination of cause.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: The sharp rise in fatalities makes the June Aster fire a major Philippine maritime disaster and raises urgent questions about vessel fire protection, evacuation procedures, passenger accounting, crew response, inspections and regulatory enforcement.

For affected families, identification of recovered remains and locating the people still missing remain the immediate priorities. For regulators and investigators, the central question is whether the disaster resulted from equipment failure, cargo conditions, operational failures, safety violations or another cause supported by evidence.

sections.heading: What remains unclear
paragraphs: The identities of all recovered victims have not yet been publicly reconciled, and 13 people remain missing in the latest verified accounting.
The cause and point of origin of the fire remain under investigation. The status and role of the vessel's captain and crew are also subjects of continuing official inquiry.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for final victim identification, recovery or accounting of the remaining missing people, Philippine Coast Guard and MARINA findings on the fire's origin and emergency response, and any administrative, civil or criminal action arising from the investigation.

sections.heading: Reader note
paragraphs: This is a developing story. FMB News will update this report as verified information becomes available.
